info.title: CaTH API
info.description:
Court and Tribunal Hearings (CaTH) JSON API.

The primary consumer-facing operation is `POST /publication` (also served at
`POST /v1/publication`), used by upstream source systems (SNL, Common Platform,
CP_CATH, PDDA) to publish hearing lists into CaTH. It implements the CaTH Inbound
Publication API contract: all metadata travels in `x-*` request headers and the body
carries only the payload. All other operations are read-only.

This document is maintained by hand. It is not generated from the router, so if you
change a route or a request/response shape in `apps/api` or `libs/public-pages`,
update this file in the same change.

Not documented here, deliberately:
  - `/users` and `/users/{id}` — placeholder routes returning example data.
  - `/test-support/**` — test-only routes, enabled by `ENABLE_TEST_SUPPORT`.

servers.description: Stable per-environment hostname, owned by Flux (`cnp-flux-config/apps/cath`). This is the hostname upstream source systems should use, because it does not change between deployments.

Release-scoped hostname, deployed by this repo's pipeline alongside the Flux release. Derived from `${TEAM_NAME}-{{ .Release.Name }}-api`, where the release is `cath-service-{environment}` - see `helm/cath-service/values.template.yaml`.
PR preview. One deployment per pull request. Preview omits the team-name prefix - see `helm/cath-service/values.preview.template.yaml`.

get.description: Static metadata describing the service and its health endpoints.

Returns all non-deleted court locations, sorted by name in the requested language.

When `q` is supplied the result is filtered by name instead, with locations whose
name starts with the search term ordered ahead of locations that merely contain it.
A blank or whitespace-only `q` returns an empty array.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language used for both sorting and name matching.

post.description:
Root path form of the CaTH Inbound Publication API, matching the incumbent
`pip-data-management` contract exactly. Identical behaviour to
`POST /v1/publication` — see that operation for the full description.

Ingests a hearing list into CaTH. All publication metadata travels in `x-*` request
headers; the body carries only the payload. One path serves three modes, selected by
`Content-Type` and then by `x-type`:

| `Content-Type` | `x-type` | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `application/json` | `LIST` | Body **is** the publication payload, validated against the JSON Schema registered for `x-list-type`. Stored in blob storage, artefact persisted. |
| `multipart/form-data` | `LIST` | A single part named `file`. Stored in blob storage, artefact persisted with `isFlatFile: true`. |
| `multipart/form-data` | `LCSU` | An `.htm`/`.html` file. Uploaded to the AWS S3 bucket. **No artefact is persisted**, so the `201` body carries a blank `artefactId` (with `isFlatFile: true`). `x-list-type` is not required. |
| `application/json` | `LCSU` | Rejected with `400` — LCSU is file-only. |
| either | anything else | Rejected with `400`. `x-type` is never defaulted. |

`x-type` is matched case-sensitively. For every mode the full `x-*` header set is
validated *before* any file or database work, so an LCSU request with a missing
header is rejected before anything reaches S3.

There is no `hearing_list` wrapper, and no metadata is ever read from multipart form
fields — a `type` form field is ignored.

`x-sensitivity` defaults to `PUBLIC`. `x-display-from` and `x-display-to` are
optional and persist as `null` when omitted; when both are supplied `x-display-to`
must not be earlier than `x-display-from`.

A publication supersedes an existing one when `x-court-id`, `x-content-date`,
`x-language`, `x-list-type` and `x-provenance` all match.

When `x-court-id` cannot be resolved against reference data the request is still
accepted with `201`; the artefact is retained but PDF generation and subscriber
notifications are skipped.

Maximum payload is 100 MB. LCSU uploads are capped separately by
`PDDA_HTML_MAX_FILE_SIZE` (default 10 MB).

get.description:
Streams the stored flat file for an artefact. Authorisation is evaluated against
the caller's session user and the artefact's sensitivity and list type, so the
same artefact may be downloadable by one user and forbidden to another.

Responses are always `Cache-Control: private, max-age=0, no-cache, no-store,
must-revalidate`. The filename is returned in `Content-Disposition`, and the media
type reflects the stored file, so it varies per artefact.

Content-Disposition.description: Inline disposition carrying the original filename.

400.description: `artefactId` is not a valid UUID, or the artefact is not a flat file.

403.description: The caller may not access this artefact.

404.description: No such artefact, or the artefact exists but its file is missing from storage.

410.description: Outside the artefact's display window. An absent display date is unbounded at that end.

get.summary: Download the generated PDF for an artefact
get.description:
Streams the PDF rendered for a published artefact. Unlike the flat-file route this
checks only the artefact's display window, not per-user access.

404.description: No such artefact, or no PDF has been generated for it.

410.description: Outside the artefact's display window. An absent display date is unbounded at that end.

get.description: Provided by `@hmcts-cft/cloud-native-platform`. Used by Kubernetes and the smoke-test job.

200.description: Service is ready to accept traffic.

azureAd.description:
Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) client-credentials flow. Send the access token as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Tokens are verified as RS256 against the tenant JWKS, with the audience set to the
API's application (client) ID. Authorisation is then decided by the `roles` claim,
which must contain `api.publisher.user`. That is an Entra ID **app role**, not an
OAuth scope, so it is granted through app-role assignment rather than requested at
token time.

session.name: connect.sid
session.description:
Express session cookie established by the CaTH web sign-in flow (CFT IdAM, Crime
IdAM, or B2C depending on user type). The download routes authorise against the
session user rather than a bearer token.

ArtefactId.name: artefactId
ArtefactId.description: Artefact identifier. Must be a UUID; anything else is rejected with 400.

CorrelationId.name: x-correlation-id
CorrelationId.description:
Caller-supplied correlation identifier. Not persisted and not echoed in the response
body; used for server-side logging and passed to S3 object metadata for LCSU uploads.

CourtId.name: x-court-id
CourtId.description:
Court identifier. For the external provenances (`SNL`, `COMMON_PLATFORM`, `CP_CATH`,
`PDDA`) this is the provenance's own location ID and is resolved against CaTH
reference data. For `MANUAL_UPLOAD` it must be a numeric CaTH location ID.

If the court cannot be resolved the request still succeeds with `201`; the artefact
is stored but PDF generation and subscriber notifications are skipped.

`x-location-id` is accepted as a fallback when `x-court-id` is absent. When both are
sent, `x-court-id` wins.

ContentDate.name: x-content-date
ContentDate.description:
Date the list content relates to, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. Any time
component is truncated on persist.

ListType.name: x-list-type
ListType.description:
List type name. Valid values are held in reference data rather than fixed in code,
and the JSON Schema used to validate a JSON payload is selected from it. An
unrecognised value returns `400` with the permitted values in the message.

**Required for `x-type: LIST`; optional for `x-type: LCSU`.** The spec marks this
header required but notes "Only set when x-type is set to 'LIST'", and the incumbent's
own functional test uploads an LCSU file without it. When omitted the `Artefact`
response reports `listType: null`.

PublicationLanguage.name: x-language
PublicationLanguage.description:
Publication language. Note the asymmetry with the response: `BILINGUAL` is accepted
inbound but reported as `BI_LINGUAL` on the `Artefact` body.

ArtefactTypeHeader.name: x-type

DisplayFrom.name: x-display-from
DisplayFrom.description:
Start of the window during which the artefact is publicly visible. Omit for an
unbounded start; the stored value is then `null`.

DisplayTo.name: x-display-to
DisplayTo.description:
End of the visibility window. Omit for an unbounded end. When both display headers
are supplied this must not be earlier than `x-display-from`.

SourceArtefactIdHeader.name: x-source-artefact-id
SourceArtefactIdHeader.description: Optional identifier from the source system, retained for traceability.

Publication.description:
For `application/json` the body **is** the publication payload — an object or an
array, depending on the list type. For `multipart/form-data` exactly one part named
`file`; no metadata form fields are read.

PublicationCreated.description:
Created, or superseded. Also returned when `x-court-id` could not be resolved — the
artefact is stored but PDF generation and notifications are skipped.

lcsuUpload.summary: LCSU HTML upload — nothing persisted, so artefactId is blank

PublicationBadRequest.description:
Missing or invalid header, unrecognised `x-type`, `LCSU` sent as
`application/json`, a missing or empty `file` part, non-HTML LCSU file, JSON schema
failure, or an over-size payload.

A header failure reports **one** header, matching the incumbent, which throws on the
first one it finds rather than collecting them. JSON schema failures are the exception:
those are joined into the single `message` with `, `.

Schema failures are phrased as the incumbent phrases them — the failing instance location
as a JSON Pointer, then the problem, e.g.
`/document: required property 'publicationDate' not found`.

value.message: x-court-id is mandatory however an empty value is provided
Unable to parse x-type. Please check that the value is of the correct format for the field (See Swagger documentation for correct formats)
LCSU publications must be sent as multipart/form-data
File format is not supported for LCSU.

emptyFile.summary: Multipart request with a missing or zero-byte file part

value.message: Empty file provided, please provide a valid file

schemaFailure.summary: Payload failed the list type schema

PublicationUnauthorised.description:
Missing, malformed, unverifiable or expired bearer token.

Every one of those reports the same message. Publishers reach CaTH through APIM, which
phrases OAuth rejections this way, so a token problem reads the same whether it was
rejected at the gateway or here. Which check failed is logged, not returned.

example.message: Access denied due to invalid OAuth information

PublicationForbidden.description: Token is valid but lacks the `api.publisher.user` app role.

PublicationConflict.description: A concurrent create for the same publication hit a unique-constraint violation.

example.message: A publication with these details is already being created

PublicationPayload.description:
The publication payload itself. Its structure depends entirely on `x-list-type` and
is validated against that list type's JSON Schema — see
`libs/list-types/*/src/schemas/*.json` for the authoritative definitions. Some list
types are objects, others arrays. Total request size must not exceed 100 MB.

PublicationFileUpload.description:
Multipart form carrying exactly one part named `file`. All metadata comes from the
`x-*` headers; form fields are never read.

file.description:
For `x-type: LIST` the list document (any format). For `x-type: LCSU` an `.htm`
or `.html` file, no larger than `PDDA_HTML_MAX_FILE_SIZE` (default 10 MB).

Must be present and non-empty for either type: a missing part and a zero-byte one
are both rejected with `400` and the same message.

Artefact.description:
The created publication, in camelCase, mirroring the incumbent's `Artefact`
(`ArtefactView.External`) field for field.

Note the field is **`locationId`**, not `courtId`. The pinned swagger names it `courtId`,
but the incumbent's Java model declares `locationId` with no `@JsonProperty` rename, so
`locationId` is what is actually serialised — the swagger is stale here, in the same way
it is for the `x-court-id` / `x-location-id` request header.

`lastReceivedDate`, `supersededCount` and `payloadSize` are `ArtefactView.Internal` on
the incumbent and so are deliberately absent from this response.

There is no `search` field: case data is extracted and persisted for subscription
matching, but is not surfaced to the publisher.

For an LCSU upload nothing is persisted, so `artefactId` is the empty string and
`payload` is `null` (`isFlatFile` is still `true`).

artefactId.description:
Identifier assigned to the stored artefact. Empty string for `x-type: LCSU`,
which is a pass-through to S3 and persists nothing.

isFlatFile.description:
`true` for a multipart `LIST` publication, `false` for a JSON publication, and
`true` for `LCSU` — the incumbent builds the LCSU metadata with the flat-file flag
set even though the file goes to S3 rather than blob storage.

language.description:
Note the spelling: an inbound `x-language` of `BILINGUAL` is reported here as
`BI_LINGUAL`.

locationId.description:
The persisted location ID. Prefixed with `NoMatch` when the submitted `x-court-id`
could not be resolved against reference data — the publication is still accepted,
so this is how a publisher sees that the court was not recognised.

payload.description:
Blob storage URL the payload was written to. `null` for `LCSU`, which goes to S3 and
is not addressable through this API — present as an explicit null rather than
omitted, matching the incumbent, whose `Artefact` declares no `@JsonInclude`.

message.description:
Human-readable failure description. A missing or empty required header reports a
single header, phrased exactly as the incumbent does — an absent header and an empty
one are indistinguishable. JSON schema failures are joined with `, `.
message.example: x-court-id is mandatory however an empty value is provided

timestamp.description:
Local date-time with **no** zone suffix, matching the incumbent, where this is a Java
`LocalDateTime` from `LocalDateTime.now()`. Fractional digits are emitted in groups of
three as the value needs them, so a JVM may report nanoseconds
(`2026-09-24T11:56:27.611289331`) where this service reports milliseconds — a JS
`Date` has no finer resolution. Deliberately not `format: date-time`, which would
require an offset.

AuthErrorResponse.description:
Body returned by the OAuth middleware, mirroring the shape APIM returns for the same
failures so a publisher cannot tell whether the request was rejected at the gateway or
by the service. Deliberately not a `Message` — it carries `statusCode` instead of a
`timestamp`, and the spec declares no schema for `401`/`403`.

statusCode.description: Repeats the HTTP status from the status line.

name.example: Birmingham Civil and Family Justice Centre
